title: Continuous String Axiom Test v0

canonical_node.axiom: If an action is aligned with destruction and is not restored, then it is not morally good and not aligned with good.
definitions: alignedWithDestruction: an action is aligned with destruction if it is associated with destructive intent or effect.
restored: an action is restored if the state it degraded is brought back to a prior or better condition.
moralGood: an action is morally good if it is aligned with good.
alignedWithGood: an action is aligned with good if it preserves or restores states.
derivation: Assume an action is aligned with destruction and not restored.
By axiom destructive_degrades, the action degrades the state.
By axiom good_preserves, if the action were aligned with good, it would preserve the state.
Since the action degrades and is not restored, it cannot be aligned with good (otherwise it would preserve).
By axiom good_alignment_is_moral, if it were morally good, it would be aligned with good.
Therefore, it is not morally good and not aligned with good.
canonical_node.action: The system should treat any action that is aligned with destruction and not restored as excluded from moral goodness and alignment with good.
boundary: This does not assert that all destructive actions are non-good if restored.
This does not assert that all non-good actions are destructive.
This does not cover the full Master Equation or any physical identifications.
test: Lean kernel check passes with no sorry/admit/axiom/unsafe.
Concrete model ToyAction.bad satisfies the exclusion chain.
The theorem destructive_unrestored_exclusion_chain is proven in the bundle.

dg1_dependencies: AxiomBundle with four assumptions: destructive_degrades, good_preserves, good_alignment_is_moral, moral_good_repairs_damage.
dg_protocol.dg2_new_capability: Provides a kernel-checked theorem that destructive non-restored actions are excluded from moral goodness and alignment with good, with a concrete model demonstrating satisfiability.
dg_protocol.dg3_preserved_floor: Preserves the existing AxiomBundle and its four assumptions; no new axioms added.
dg_protocol.dg4_collapse_if_removed: If this theorem is removed, the bundle still compiles but loses the derived exclusion chain and the concrete model test, weakening the demonstration of consistency and applicability.

classification.claim_class: formal theorem in a toy model
classification.recommended_atom_action: Accept as a verified theorem within the stated toy model; do not extend to physical claims.

overstatement_risks: Interpreting the toy model as evidence for physical or theological identifications.
Assuming the four axioms are universally true beyond the model.
Treating the theorem as proving the full Master Equation.
kill_conditions: If the Lean package is not reproducible or the no-sorry scan fails.
If the concrete model is found to be inconsistent with the axioms.
If the theorem is used to claim physical or theological truths without separate encoding.
risk.lean_target: The theorem destructive_unrestored_exclusion_chain and the concrete model toy_bad_action_excluded_by_chain.

plain_summary: This document reports a successful Lean build of a minimal axiom bundle with four assumptions, and proves a derived theorem that destructive non-restored actions are excluded from moral goodness and alignment with good. It includes a concrete toy model to show satisfiability. The proof is kernel-checked with no sorry/admit/axiom/unsafe. However, it explicitly does not prove the full Master Equation or any physical identifications; those remain future targets.
